questions.q: Pedagogy can be defined as a way of ____ any theoretical topic or academic subject.
questions.explanation: Pedagogy is the method and practice of teaching, i.e. the way a teacher teaches a theoretical topic or academic subject.

options: enabling self to be good at rote memorization
questions.explanation: Good pedagogy aims at real understanding, so it elicits responses from learners that demonstrate understanding. Rote memorization and hampering cognitive development are the opposite of good pedagogy.

questions.q: Which of the following is a pedagogical approach in teaching?
questions.explanation: Integrative pedagogy, which connects ideas across topics and disciplines, is one of the pedagogical approaches discussed alongside constructivist, collaborative, reflective and inquiry-based approaches.

questions.q: According to the ____ approach, learners are the makers of meaning and knowledge.
questions.explanation: Constructivist learning holds that learners actively construct their own meaning and knowledge from experience rather than passively receiving it.

questions.q: Which of the following is false about inquiry-based learning?
options: is a form of passive learning
generally used in small scale investigations
questions.explanation: Inquiry-based learning is a form of active learning that starts by posing questions or problems and includes problem-based learning, so calling it passive is false.

questions.q: The ____ model describes what effective teachers do in their classrooms to engage students in intellectually challenging work.
questions.explanation: The Pedagogical Model describes what effective teachers do in their classrooms to engage students in intellectually challenging work, breaking the learning cycle into phases of instruction.

questions.q: In experiential learning, experiences are structured to require the student to ____.
questions.explanation: Experiential learning structures experiences so that students must take initiative, make decisions and be accountable for the results, so all the options apply.

questions.q: The following are the roles of an instructor in experiential learning, except ____.
questions.explanation: In experiential learning the instructor sets suitable experiences, poses problems, sets boundaries and supports students. Blurring the boundaries is not one of the instructor's roles; setting clear boundaries is.

questions.q: Kolb's experiential learning style theory is typically represented by a ____-stage learning cycle
questions.explanation: Kolb's cycle has four stages: concrete experience, reflective observation, abstract conceptualization and active experimentation.

questions.q: People with ____ learning style are hands-on learners, and rely on intuition over logic.
questions.explanation: Kolb's accommodating (doing and feeling) style is hands-on and intuitive; such learners rely on intuition and gut feeling more than logic. Converging learners, by contrast, prefer technical problem solving and practical application of ideas.
